title: Backward-facing step, Re_D = 100 (Armaly et al.), Hex-dominant (2D)

setup.words: A backward-facing step channel: an inlet channel h = 5.2 mm high and 52 mm long on top of a step S = 4.9 mm, then a channel H = 10.1 mm high and 303 mm (30 H) long after it (expansion ratio 1.942), 5 mm deep in z (one cell across) (STEP in mm, built with OCP: two boxes fused and unified); a custom fluid with nu = 0.000104 m²/s and rho = 1 kg/m³, so Re_D = U_b 2h / nu = 100; a uniform velocity inlet of 1 m/s normal to the face, a 0 Pa pressure outlet, every wall no-slip (the floor after the step and the top wall BCs of their own), the front and back one Symmetry (the 2D mesh's ends, solved empty); laminar, steady (simpleFoam), Accurate numerics, residual targets 1e-6, at most 4000 iterations.

geometry.builder: backward-facing step channel: an inlet channel h = 5.2 mm high and 52 mm long on top of a step S = 4.9 mm, then a channel H = 10.1 mm high and 303 mm (30 H) long after it (expansion ratio 1.942), 5 mm deep in z (one cell across)

estimate.n_cells_note: an order of magnitude of the 2D mesh (one cell across), not a prediction

setup.mesh_words: Hex-dominant at fineness 10, One cell across (2D) on, a custom size of 0.3 mm on every wall with Refine out to 5.05 mm (half the height: the whole channel), no wall layers; 1 non-orthogonal corrector

rows.text: The run starts from rest; starting from potential flow shortens the start-up.

estimate.line: 4,000 iterations at most · ~21 minutes on 8 cores · Re ≈ 100

histories.label: U_x in the floor's bubble (the first Bubble probe)

quantities.label: Primary reattachment on the floor, x1/S (Re_D 100)

uncertainty.what: half the spacing of the two face centres around the zero

quantities.how: the x component of the wall shear stress the run saved on the floor after the step (wallShearStress, one face per x on the 2D mesh), its sign in the attached flow far after the step (0.6 to 0.9 of the length after it) taken as forward; x1 where it turns from reversed to forward at the end of its longest reversed stretch, the primary eddy from the step's foot (a corner eddy's forward flow at the foot, if any, is passed over), the zero linearly interpolated between the two face centres around it; over the step height S

reference.citation: B. F. Armaly, F. Durst, J. C. F. Pereira, B. Schonung (1983), "Experimental and theoretical investigation of backward-facing step flow", J. Fluid Mech. 127:473-496
reference.where: Fig. 14 at Re = 100, the measured primary reattachment x1/S (validation/refs/armaly_1983_fig14_x1.csv)
reference.conditions: backward-facing step, expansion ratio 1:1.94 (downstream channel 10.1 mm high, aspect ratio 18:1; inlet channel h about 5.2 mm and step S about 4.9 mm, derived); Re = V D / nu with V the mean inlet velocity (two-thirds of the measured maximum) and D = 2h the inlet channel's hydraulic diameter; air, laser-Doppler measurements; x1 from the step
reference.note: The flow was two-dimensional only for Re < 400 (and Re > 6000); from Re 453 upward the values are three-dimensional-affected and Armaly's own 2D predictions are no reference above Re about 400 (pp. 474, 489-490, 493)

tolerance.note: the reference data's band: the experiment, the digitising and the expansion ratio

quantities.detail: x = 13.986 mm (1.385 H) between face centres 0.174 mm apart; 1746 floor faces
